description: Hi guys! Looking for teammates:) Highly interested in web developers and somebody interested in agriculture and weather forecasting.
summary: A web-based decision-support system, based on custom-built recommendation engine, complemented by SI-based predictions of environment. It provides farmers with ability to make informed decisions, based on crops, that were growing on this field before, predicted air temperature, precipitation, root zone soil wellness, solar radiation and relative humidity for 19 different crop types.
details:
Peter67's Farm is a web app for the NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data". The user outlines a field on a satellite map. The app shows which crops grew there in past seasons (US only, from USDA Cropland Data Layer) and ranks crops for the next season with sowing windows and reasons. It proposes three-year rotation plans that can be ranked by water saving, soil building or erosion control. A Climate tab shows daily NASA POWER data and a 12-month outlook of whether temperature, humidity and soil wetness will be below, near or above normal.

The crop advice combines agronomy rules with a model. The rules take sowing dates from NASA POWER climate normals, the growing cycle from thermal time, and suitability from temperature and water needs. They add frost risk, soil pH from SSURGO or SoilGrids, and rotation penalties and bonuses. In the US, a gradient boosting model trained on CDL crop sequences predicts the next crop, and the final score is half model, half rules. With whole fields held out, it reaches 67.2% accuracy against 64.1% for a lookup baseline, and the right crop is in its top 3 in 92.5% of cases. Elsewhere the rules work alone. The outlook uses a gradient boosting classifier per variable, trained on NASA POWER history and NASA GEOS-S2S forecasts. A backtest checks each month ahead, and months without proven skill show an even 1/3 for each outcome.

The app uses only public data, so a farmer needs no sensors or records. It is meant to help farmers adapt crop choices to local climate, water and soil, and to support a decision, not replace an agronomist.

The frontend is React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind and Leaflet. The backend is .NET 10 with MediatR, EF Core and PostgreSQL, using JWT auth. The model service is Python with FastAPI, scikit-learn, pandas and rasterio. .NET Aspire runs everything locally, and production is Docker Compose with Caddy on one VM, deployed by GitHub Actions. There is no special hardware.

The model learns common practice, not the best practice. Crop advice uses climate normals, not a seasonal forecast. CDL lags the calendar, so users can report their last crop. Markets, equipment and irrigation capacity are not modelled. The first outlook request for an area waits while the model trains.
